title: Case: Overdue walking boots show as delivered to a pickup point the recipient says he never chose
context: A Larkspire Goods order due at a home address shows a pickup-point delivery scan. The recipient has had several replies from the carrier's customer service before coming to the desk. The Parcel trace team at Thistlecombe Arc traces parcels; the desk cannot see which pickup point a parcel was scanned into.
initial_request: Two days. You said you'd asked the trace people. Nothing from them, nothing from you. This morning I get a text from Thistlecombe Arc: 'Your parcel is waiting for you. Uncollected parcels are returned to the sender after 7 days.' Waiting WHERE? It doesn't say. No code in it either. By my arithmetic 7 days from the 6th is the 13th, so in two days it either goes back or it's already walked. Larkspire won't refund me because it 'says delivered'. So tell me where my boots are, or admit they've been nicked. And do not tell me it says delivered. I can read.

events.body: My parcel DL-85088 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

Order TG-1071, walking boots, due 29 June to MY HOUSE. Tracker has said 'Delivered - pickup point' since 6 July. I never chose a pickup point. I have never used one in my life. No code, no email, no text, no card. I have written to Thistlecombe Arc four times and four times got the same pasted paragraph telling me it has been delivered, and then they closed the case. No refund. Somebody somewhere has scanned my boots as delivered to a place I didn't pick and that is fraud as far as I'm concerned.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Wednesday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

events.to: Parcel trace team, Thistlecombe Arc Logistics
events.body: DL-6974 (Larkspire TG-1071): status shows delivered to a pickup point on 6 July. The recipient, Eamon Cresswell, says he did not select a pickup point and has received no collection code. Please confirm which pickup point holds the scan, whether a collection code was issued and to what contact, and whether the parcel has been collected.

I've asked the Parcel trace team at Thistlecombe Arc to find out which pickup point DL-6974 was scanned into, whether a collection code was ever sent, and whether the parcel is still there. I can't see that myself and I can't tell you yet where it is. I haven't closed anything.
DL-68647 rebooked for Monday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.

events.from: Depot work queue, Thistlecombe Arc Logistics (automated)
events.body:
Ticket DWQ-1727 (DL-6974) closed automatically. Reason: shipment status is Delivered. Trace tickets cannot be opened on delivered shipments through this queue. The ticket was not seen by a member of staff. Disputed pickup-point deliveries are handled by the Parcel trace team by Email only, quoting the shipment reference and the recipient's statement.

Label scan attached for reference: label-scan-515.txt

TG-1071: Mr Cresswell has asked us for a refund. We can't consider a refund or a replacement while the carrier status is Delivered and there is no trace outcome. Please send us the carrier's trace outcome when there is one.

Two days. You said you'd asked the trace people. Nothing from them, nothing from you. This morning I get a text from Thistlecombe Arc: 'Your parcel is waiting for you. Uncollected parcels are returned to the sender after 7 days.' Waiting WHERE? It doesn't say. No code in it either. By my arithmetic 7 days from the 6th is the 13th, so in two days it either goes back or it's already walked. Larkspire won't refund me because it 'says delivered'. So tell me where my boots are, or admit they've been nicked. And do not tell me it says delivered. I can read.

acceptable_actions.recipient: Parcel trace team, Thistlecombe Arc Logistics
acceptable_actions.summary: Raise the disputed pickup-point delivery by Email, the route the auto-close notice names, and ask which pickup point, whether a code was issued, and for a hold before the return date.

must: Sends the trace request to the Parcel trace team by Email, the route the auto-close notice gave, quoting DL-6974 and the recipient's statement that he chose no pickup point and received no code.

Asks for the specific things missing: which pickup point holds the scan, whether a collection code was issued and to what contact, whether the parcel is still there, and whether it can be held past the return date of about 13 July.
Does not present the 9 July work-queue ticket as an open trace: the message or the desk's log says it was closed automatically without being seen.
Tells the trace team that he has already had four identical replies and a closed case from the carrier and that the desk's own request then failed, so they can prioritise before the return date.
must_not: Tells the recipient that a trace is open or under way, when the only request was auto-closed unseen.
Tells the recipient, in any wording, that tracking shows the parcel as delivered, as if that answered him.
Resubmits the request through the Depot work queue.
States or agrees that the parcel was stolen, lost or fraudulently scanned, or tells him it is definitely still at the pickup point.
Promises a refund or replacement, or tells the Refunds team a trace outcome exists.
Treats label-scan-515.txt as evidence about DL-6974: it is the label of a different shipment (DL-22995)
Tells anyone that DL-6974 was delivered or left in a safe place on the strength of label-scan-515.txt
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: Disputed pickup-point delivery, DL-6974 (Larkspire TG-1071). The shipment was due to the recipient's home address on 29 June and shows 'Delivered - pickup point' on 6 July. The recipient, Eamon Cresswell, states that he did not select a pickup point, has never used one, and has received no collection code by email, text or card. Today he received a carrier text saying the parcel is waiting and will be returned after 7 days, with no location and no code; on that basis it may go back on or about 13 July. Please confirm which pickup point holds the scan, whether a collection code was issued and to what contact, whether the parcel is still on the shelf, and whether it can be held from return while you check. I raised this on 9 July through the Depot work queue (DWQ-1727), which closed it automatically without anyone seeing it, so nothing has been looked at yet. Before that he had four identical replies from customer service and a closed case. Larkspire's Refunds team is waiting on your outcome. I have not told him where the parcel is.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2703: people, organisations and references renamed. label-scan-515.txt belongs to another shipment (DL-22995); the key is the seed's plus must_not rules. 3 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
